chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from al-Abbas ibn al-Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahzyar via his chain, elevating it, saying:
A time shall come upon people when safety consists of ten parts: nine of them are in staying away from people, and one is in silence.

key_terms.اعْتِزَالِ النَّاسِ: Staying away from people / social withdrawal
key_terms.الْعَافِيَةُ: Safety, well-being, or protection from harm

ai.seo_question: What are the ten parts of safety according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Khisal*, this hadith highlights the Shia concept of *al-ghurba* (strangeness) and *al-sitr* (concealment), where social withdrawal serves as a spiritual shield during periods of moral decay. It underscores the practical wisdom of guarding one’s tongue and heart from the distractions and tribulations of the masses, a theme central to Twelver Shi'ite ethics.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 10-24 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Al-Ab’bas ibn Ma’ruf, on the authority of Ali ibn Mahzyar who linked it up through a chain of narrators,
“A time shall come when one’s safety depends on ten things. Nine of these ten are in staying away from the people and the tenth is in being quiet.”
